about.title: Portola Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Portola is a town of just under 1,900 people, and a sudden loss here is felt on every block. In 2025, public records show two injury collisions in the city, three people hurt, and no traffic deaths. That count is a relief, but it does not cover every way a family can lose someone: a fall at a business, an error in medical care, a workplace incident, or a crash on Rt 70, Grizzly Road, or 5th Avenue that ends in a hospital elsewhere. A wrongful death claim is a civil matter, entirely separate from any criminal charges the district attorney may or may not bring. Under California law, the spouse or domestic partner and children generally have the first right to file, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The claim can seek funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and compensation for the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Most families have two years from the date of death to act, and less time if a public agency is involved. LawProactive simply connects you with an attorney who can explain where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Portola Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, starting with the spouse or domestic partner and children. The attorney you are connected with can explain whether you, or another family member, has standing.

items.title: Deadlines that will not wait
items.desc: The general limit is two years from the date of death, but claims involving a city, county, or state agency require much faster notice. Getting connected early protects your right to file at all.

items.title: No cost to connect, no fee without recovery

items.question: The crash happened on Rt 70 near Portola. Does it matter that the road is a state highway?
items.answer: It can. If a road condition, signage, or maintenance issue played a role, a claim might involve Caltrans or another public agency, and claims against government entities in California carry a much shorter notice deadline than the standard two years. An attorney can look at the facts and tell you whether that applies to your situation. Most cases still focus on the drivers involved, but it is worth checking early.

items.question: There is already a criminal case. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, they are separate. A criminal case is brought by the prosecutor and focuses on punishment; it does not pay for funeral costs, lost income, or the loss of your loved one's companionship. A wrongful death claim is the civil path for the family to recover those losses. The two can proceed at the same time.

items.question: What can our family actually recover in a California wrongful death claim?
items.answer: Recoverable losses generally include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have contributed over their lifetime, and the loss of their love, companionship, comfort, and guidance. The specific amount depends on the facts of your case and cannot be predicted in advance. An attorney can walk you through how these categories apply to your family.
